derived_by: same reproduce worker, separate algebraic pass without importing input-a.json or source phase values
starting_assumptions: M is a nonnegative real 3x3 matrix with every row and column sum equal to one
probability columns are inputs and rows are outputs
only columns 0 and 1 are selected initially
derivation: Column normalization gives two unit vectors with the prescribed moduli.
After row rephasing, their inner product is a sum of three complex numbers of moduli L0,L1,L2.
Such a sum can vanish exactly iff the three nonnegative lengths close, equivalently 2*max(Li) <= sum(Li).
Any orthonormal pair in C^3 has a one-dimensional orthogonal complement. Completing with its unit vector gives a unitary.
For every row i, completeness gives |u_i2|^2 = 1-M_i0-M_i1 = M_i2, using the row sum. Thus the completion has all prescribed moduli.

branch_rules.three_positive: strict or saturated triangle; cosine-law phases may be used
branch_rules.exactly_two_positive: closure iff the two positive lengths are equal; use opposite phases
branch_rules.all_zero: orthogonality sum is identically zero; complete the two normalized columns directly

scope_note: This derives the exact order-three input-admissibility criterion only; it does not resolve closure under multiplication.
